limits: Laws are proved about the generated Bend model, not about the Python runtime or its SQLite adapter.
The model abstracts version (CAS), operation replay, audit persistence, crash durability and the HTTP layer.

Effect emission is modelled as 'a successful step emits exactly its rule's declared effects'; the runtime's additional EFFECT_DENIED rejection of unknown effect kinds is not modelled (the model is more permissive).
Conformance to the runtime is a bounded differential test (matrix cells and traces), not a proof.
The unsafe models are a fixed set of seeded faults; failing them shows sensitivity to those faults only.
The laws are authored by the same team as the model; they are not an independently blinded specification.

laws.name: teacher_never_approves
laws.statement: LAW 1: whatever a Teacher does (active or not, assigned or not), in any state and in either model, the accepted command never leaves the instance Approved.

laws.name: teacher_sequences_never_approve
laws.statement: LAW 2: no sequence of commands issued only by teachers can ever reach Approved from the initial state.

laws.name: approved_only_from_recommended
laws.statement: LAW 3: in the recommend_only candidate, any accepted command into Approved fires from Recommended.

laws.name: every_path_to_approved_passes_recommended
laws.statement: LAW 4: in the candidate, every path to Approved passes through Recommended (all sequences, any actors).

laws.name: revoked_teacher_cannot_recommend
laws.statement: LAW 5: a revoked teacher can never recommend, whatever their assignment and whatever the state.

laws.name: unassigned_teacher_cannot_recommend
laws.statement: LAW 6: an unassigned teacher can never recommend, whether or not they are active.

laws.name: reject_only_from_declared_source
laws.statement: LAW 7: Reject is accepted only from the declared rejection source of the model.

laws.name: forbidden_effects_never_emitted
laws.statement: LAW 8: no command, by any actor in any state, ever emits a forbidden effect.
